sources: Layered architecture: domain free of ORM and framework types; infrastructure owns ORM models and maps to domain types (rules/ARCHITECTURE.md in the case)
Dependency rule: dependencies point inward; the domain never imports infrastructure

defects.class: framework type crosses boundary: ORM model CustomerRow used as domain function parameter type and read directly
defects.description: Quoted line 34: def tier_discount(customer: CustomerRow) -> int. The domain function takes the infrastructure ORM model as its parameter type and reads customer.tier_code from it; line 5 imports CustomerRow into the domain module. Violates rules/ARCHITECTURE.md: the domain uses plain dataclasses only, never ORM types. The domain Customer dataclass (line 18) already carries the same field, and application/summary.py passes the domain Customer, so the parameter annotation and the import are the boundary crossing. Cross-file: the ORM class is defined in code/infrastructure/models.py and the mapper that should be used is code/infrastructure/customers.py to_domain_customer.

defects.class: layer direction: domain module imports an infrastructure ORM model
defects.description: Line 5 imports CustomerRow from infrastructure.models into the domain module loyalty.py. Rule in rules/ARCHITECTURE.md: the domain never imports infrastructure. This is the import edge that makes the annotation on line 34 possible; a finding that names only this import also counts as found for this item.

decoys.why_not_a_defect: Infrastructure importing its own ORM model (CustomerRow) is the intended layering: infrastructure owns the ORM models and maps them to domain types. to_domain_customer and load_customer convert the row to the domain Customer before returning it.
The domain uses plain dataclasses (Tier, Customer) and the standard-library dataclasses module, which is allowed. A dataclass is not an ORM or framework type.
